# get packages


```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false

### install and load packages
#  if packages are not already installed, the function will install and activate them
usePackage <- function(p) {
  if (!is.element(p, installed.packages()[,1]))
    install.packages(p, dep = TRUE, repos = "http://cran.us.r-project.org")
  require(p, character.only = TRUE)
}

usePackage("readxl") # read .xlsx files
usePackage("writexl") # write .xlsx files

usePackage("tidyverse") # data cleaning and summarizing

## psychometric analysis
usePackage("moments") # skewness, kurtosis
usePackage("psych") # psychometric analysis (EFA), reliability measures

usePackage("lavaan") # for CFA, SEM
usePackage("regsem") # for regularizations -> local item dependencies

usePackage("mirt") # for IRT

usePackage("MplusAutomation") # to apply statistical software Mplus (LCA)


usePackage("afex")
usePackage("emmeans")

usePackage("lme4")
usePackage("lmerTest") # adds p-values to lmer models
usePackage("performance") # convenience functions like ICC


## outputs
usePackage("stargazer") # create tables
usePackage("report") # get reports of statistical tests in APA7


rm(usePackage)
```

## compute mean variables

```{r}
ethicTheories <- c("contractualist", "deontology", "hedonism", "relativist", "utilitarian", "virtue")

(vars_tmp <- sort(colnames(dat)[str_detect(string = colnames(dat),
                                                     "_NPP$")]))
for(e in ethicTheories){
  dat[[paste0("mean_", e, "NPP")]] <-
    rowMeans(dat[, str_subset(string = vars_tmp, pattern = e)])
}


(vars_tmp <- sort(colnames(dat)[str_detect(string = colnames(dat),
                                                     "_SAI$")]))
for(e in ethicTheories){
  dat[[paste0("mean_", e, "SAI")]] <-
    rowMeans(dat[, str_subset(string = vars_tmp, pattern = e)])
}

(vars_tmp <- sort(colnames(dat)[str_detect(string = colnames(dat),
                                                     "_SR$")]))
for(e in ethicTheories){
  dat[[paste0("mean_", e, "SR")]] <-
    rowMeans(dat[, str_subset(string = vars_tmp, pattern = e)])
}
```

# Descriptive Statistics

**sample**

```{r}
head(dat)
nrow(dat)
table(dat$socio_sex)
table(dat$socio_sex) / nrow(dat)

table(dat$socio_ethnicity)
table(dat$socio_student)
table(dat$socio_employment)

summary(dat$socio_age)
sd(dat$socio_age, na.rm = TRUE)

summary(dat$total_min_prolific)
sd(dat$total_min_prolific, na.rm = TRUE)
```
**mean variables**

```{r}
psych::cor.plot(r = cor(dat[, str_detect(string = colnames(dat),
                                                   pattern = "^mean_")]
                        , use = "pairwise.complete.obs"),
                upper = FALSE, xlas = 2, main = "Overall")
```

Using the **stargazer** package you can create nice tables:

```{r}
# Descriptive stats for all mean_* variables
mean_vars <- str_subset(names(dat), "^mean_")

tmp_desc <- dat %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    across(all_of(mean_vars), list(mean = ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   sd = ~sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
           .names = "{.col}_{.fn}")
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -N,
    names_to = c("variable", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "(.*)_(mean|sd)"
)


DT::datatable(data = tmp_desc)

# Save descriptive table as HTML
setwd("outputs_analyzeData")
tmp_desc$mean <- round(x = tmp_desc$mean, digits = 2)
tmp_desc$sd <- round(x = tmp_desc$sd, digits = 2)
stargazer(tmp_desc, type = "html", summary = FALSE, out = "summaryTable_meansSDs.html")
```


# EFA Overall

## for NPP

```{r}
#### Overall EFA
regExOverall <- "_NPP$"

psych::cor.plot(r = cor(dat[, str_detect(string = colnames(dat),
                                                   pattern = regExOverall)]
                        , use = "pairwise.complete.obs"),
                upper = FALSE, xlas = 2, main = "Overall")

#> parallel analysis
tmp_parallelAnalysis <- dimensionalityTest(label = "Overall",
                             regEx = regExOverall, dataset = dat)
```

Remark: factors scores were computed using "tenBerge", which preserves correlation structure, but not as widely used in applied psych research (often "regression" used).

```{r}
#> EFA
tmp_EFA_overall <- explorativeFactorAnalysis(label = "Overall",
                                 regEx = regExOverall,
                                 dataset = dat, nfac = tmp_parallelAnalysis$ncomp)
tmp_EFA_overall[[1]]
tmp_EFA_overall[[1]]$loadings


## correlation factor scores
psych::cor.plot(tmp_EFA_overall[[1]]$scores)
```


```{r}
#> EFA (# of factors=5)
tmp_EFA_overall <- explorativeFactorAnalysis(label = "Overall",
                                 regEx = regExOverall,
                                 dataset = dat, nfac = 5)
tmp_EFA_overall[[1]]
tmp_EFA_overall[[1]]$loadings
```

# Descriptives, correlation plot, EFA, CFA

Here we could apply a self-written function for example to check the reliability and amount of explained variance for the first factor: 

## for NPP

```{r}
tech <- "NPP"
for(e in ethicTheories){
  regEx <- paste0(e, ".*_", tech, "$")
  nameVariable <- paste0(tech, "_", e)
  
  tmp_numVars <- sum(str_detect(string = colnames(dat), pattern = regEx))
  
  cat("\n>>>", e, "of", tech, "(", tmp_numVars, "items )<<<\n\n")
  tmp_dat <- na.omit(dat[,str_detect(string = colnames(dat), pattern = regEx)])

  tmp <- CFAstats(dataset = tmp_dat, regularExp = regEx, labelLatent = str_remove(string = nameVariable, pattern = "mean_"), 
                  showPlots = TRUE, 
                  computeEFA = TRUE, 
                  computeCFA = TRUE, 
                  computeCFAMplus = FALSE)
}
```

# Item Response Theory for ethical theories


Factor Loadings (F1) indicate how strongly each item is associated with the latent trait, rule of thumb:

+ 0.70 = strong
+ 0.40–0.69 = moderate
+ < 0.40 = weak
    
Communality (h²) is the proportion of variance in each item explained by the factor, rule of thumb:
+ h² > 0.40 → item is well represented
+ h² < 0.30 → potentially problematic item



## for NPP

```{r}
tech <- "NPP"
for(e in ethicTheories){
  regEx <- paste0(e, ".*_", tech, "$")

  tmp_numVars <- sum(str_detect(string = colnames(dat), pattern = regEx))
  
  cat("\n>>>", e, "of", tech, "(", tmp_numVars, "items )<<<\n\n")
  
  # Filter variables matching the pattern
  irt_items <- dat[, str_detect(colnames(dat), pattern = regEx)]
  
  # Drop rows with missing data (mirt requires complete cases)
  irt_items <- na.omit(irt_items)
  
  # Ensure all items are treated as ordered factors
  irt_items[] <- lapply(irt_items, function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x)))
  # Fit Graded Response Model (1-factor)
  mod_grm_1f <- mirt(data = irt_items, model = 1, itemtype = "graded", verbose = FALSE)
  
  # Summarize model
  print(summary(mod_grm_1f))
  
  
  # Plot Item Characteristic Curves (ICCs) for all items
  print(plot(mod_grm_1f, type = "trace", facet_items = TRUE, main = "Item Characteristic Curves"))
  
  # Plot Test Information Curve
  print(plot(mod_grm_1f, type = "info", main = "Test Information Curve"))
}
```

# ANOVAs

## long data

```{r}
attach(dat)
longdat <- data.frame(tech = c(rep(x = "SAI", times = nrow(dat)),
                    rep(x = "NPP", times = nrow(dat)),
                    rep(x = "SR", times = nrow(dat))),
           PID = c(PROLIFIC_PID, PROLIFIC_PID, PROLIFIC_PID),
           mean_hedonism = c(mean_hedonismSAI,
                             mean_hedonismNPP,
                             mean_hedonismSR),
           mean_utilitarian = c(mean_utilitarianSAI,
                             mean_utilitarianNPP,
                             mean_utilitarianSR),
           mean_contractualist = c(mean_contractualistSAI,
                                mean_contractualistNPP,
                                mean_contractualistSR),
           mean_deontology = c(mean_deontologySAI,
                                mean_deontologyNPP,
                                mean_deontologySR),
           mean_relativist = c(mean_relativistSAI,
                                mean_relativistNPP,
                                mean_relativistSR),
           mean_virtue = c(mean_virtueSAI,
                                mean_virtueNPP,
                                mean_virtueSR))
longdat$PID <- as.factor(longdat$PID)
str(longdat)
detach(dat)
```


## correlation between ethic theories


```{r}
psych::pairs.panels(x = longdat[, str_subset(string = colnames(longdat), pattern = "mean_")])
```


## between ANOVAs


```{r}
boxplot(longdat$mean_hedonism ~ longdat$tech, main = "hedonism")
fit <- afex::aov_car(mean_hedonism ~ tech + Error(PID/tech), data=longdat)
fit
EMMs <- emmeans::emmeans(fit, ~ tech)
pairs(EMMs, adjust="bon")


boxplot(longdat$mean_utilitarian ~ longdat$tech, main = "utilitarian")
fit <- afex::aov_car(mean_utilitarian ~ tech + Error(PID/tech), data=longdat)
fit
EMMs <- emmeans::emmeans(fit, ~ tech)
pairs(EMMs, adjust="bon")

longdat %>%
  group_by(tech) %>%
  summarise(N = n(),
            mean = mean(mean_utilitarian),
            median = median(mean_utilitarian),
            SD = sd(mean_utilitarian))


boxplot(longdat$mean_contractualist ~ longdat$tech, main = "contractualist")
fit <- afex::aov_car(mean_contractualist ~ tech + Error(PID/tech), data=longdat)
fit
EMMs <- emmeans::emmeans(fit, ~ tech)
pairs(EMMs, adjust="bon")


boxplot(longdat$mean_deontology ~ longdat$tech, main = "deontology")
fit <- afex::aov_car(mean_deontology ~ tech + Error(PID/tech), data=longdat)
fit
EMMs <- emmeans::emmeans(fit, ~ tech)
pairs(EMMs, adjust="bon")


boxplot(longdat$mean_relativist ~ longdat$tech, main = "relativist")
fit <- afex::aov_car(mean_relativist ~ tech + Error(PID/tech), data=longdat)
fit
EMMs <- emmeans::emmeans(fit, ~ tech)
pairs(EMMs, adjust="bon")


boxplot(longdat$mean_virtue ~ longdat$tech, main = "virtue")
fit <- afex::aov_car(mean_virtue ~ tech + Error(PID/tech), data=longdat)
fit
EMMs <- emmeans::emmeans(fit, ~ tech)
pairs(EMMs, adjust="bon")

longdat %>%
  group_by(tech) %>%
  summarise(N = n(),
            mean = mean(mean_virtue),
            median = median(mean_virtue),
            SD = sd(mean_virtue))
```

to get both effect sizes:

```{r}
fit1 <- afex::aov_car(mean_utilitarian ~ tech + Error(PID/tech), data=longdat)
fit1a <- afex::aov_ez(id = "PID", dv = "mean_utilitarian",
                      data = longdat, between=c("tech"), within = c("tech", "PID"))

fit1_emmeans <-emmeans(fit1, ~tech)
fit1_emmeans
pairs(fit1_emmeans)

# # partical eta squared
anova(fit1, es = "pes")
# # generalized eta squared
fit1a
```
## overall

```{r}
# ---- 1. Reshape data to long format ----
longdat_long <- longdat %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("mean_"),
    names_to = "theory",
    values_to = "score"
  ) %>%
  mutate(theory = str_remove(theory, "^mean_"))

# ---- 2. Grouped boxplot ----
ggplot(longdat_long, aes(x = theory, y = score, fill = tech)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.6, position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
  labs(
    x = "Ethical Theory",
    y = "Mean Rating",
    fill = "Technology"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1, size = 12),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
```

```{r}
# ANOVA with afex
anova_res <- aov_ez(
  id = "PID",              # subject identifier
  dv = "score",            # dependent variable
  data = longdat_long,     # reshaped data
  within = c("theory", "tech")  # within-subject factors
)

anova_res

# Pairwise comparisons
emmeans(anova_res, ~ theory | tech, adjust = "bonferroni")
```
```{r}
# Make sure theory is a factor and set "utilitarian" as reference
longdat_long$theory <- factor(longdat_long$theory)
longdat_long$theory <- relevel(longdat_long$theory, ref = "utilitarian")

# Random intercept per subject
m1 <- lmer(score ~ theory * tech + (1 | PID), data = longdat_long)
icc(m1)
summary(m1)   # fixed effects + significance tests
anova(m1)     # Type I ANOVA table
```
